symptom: A build-only invocation (build-run.ps1 -NoRun) killed the running Deckle before compiling, so voice dictation, the HUD and the MCP surfaces stayed down until a manual relaunch; the flag only skipped the relaunch, not the stop.
cause: The stop step ran unconditionally ahead of the build, justified by output locks, although a running instance only locks the directory it was launched from (its exe and every loaded assembly). A Debug validation build or a build in another worktree writes elsewhere and never needed the stop.
violatedInvariant: A command that only builds never changes the lifetime of the running Deckle instance; only commands that replace it (launch, build and run, clean) stop it, and they say so.

must: Leave the running instance untouched when -NoRun is set, whatever configuration or worktree is built.
Refuse a -NoRun build before compiling when the running instance lives in that build's exact output directory, naming the process, the directory and the ways out.
Keep the stop on the build-and-run path: Deckle is single-instance, so the fresh exe cannot take over while the resident holds the mutex.
mustNot: Let a build-only run fail on locked files after a full compile, which leaves the output directory half-copied.
Add a flag that stops the resident without relaunching it; that is exactly the state the incident produced.

automation.residual: The test covers the seam (Get-DeckleProcessInDirectory: same directory, sibling pivot, RID-suffixed pivot, other worktree, unreadable path, no process). Which branch build-run.ps1 takes is not exercised automatically; it was verified by running -NoRun against a checkout whose Release instance is running (refused before compiling, process untouched) and with -Configuration Debug (built, process untouched).
